outcome: maternal complications (infection, need for blood transfusion)
cohort: The study included 102 women who had previously undergone a cesarean section and were attempting a vaginal delivery.
finding: VBAC is a safe and effective option for women with a prior CS, with a high success rate (79.4%), however, VBAC failure was found to be an independent predictor of both fetal and maternal complications.
mod_finding: VBAC failure was associated with significantly higher maternal complications (infection, blood transfusion) and worse fetal outcomes (APGAR score <7 at 10 minutes) compared to VBAC success.
cross-section timing: During the attempt at vaginal birth after cesarean (TOLAC) and immediate post-birth.
